default_policy: Select the smallest set that materially changes a decision or improves execution. Read a selected SKILL.md before applying it.

capabilities.name: engineering-task-workflow
capabilities.trigger: Any non-trivial repository engineering task.
capabilities.guard: Skip for simple questions or writing unrelated to a repository.

capabilities.name: intent-driven-development
capabilities.trigger: Material ambiguity, high-impact product behavior, or acceptance criteria that cannot be inferred safely.
capabilities.guard: Do not add a discovery ceremony when the requested behavior and evidence are already clear.

capabilities.name: verification-before-completion
capabilities.trigger: Before any claim that repository work is complete, fixed, or passing.
capabilities.guard: Requires fresh evidence for the current files; implementation alone never satisfies it.

capabilities.name: tdd-workflow
capabilities.trigger: A behavior change, regression, or refactor where a focused automated test can fail meaningfully first.
capabilities.guard: Skip for documentation, generated artifacts, or tests that only mirror implementation.

capabilities.name: systematic-debugging
capabilities.trigger: A reproducible bug, failing check, regression, or unexplained behavior.
capabilities.guard: This is the only general debugging workflow; use evidence and one falsifiable hypothesis at a time.

capabilities.name: database-migrations
capabilities.trigger: Any persistent schema or data migration.
capabilities.guard: Covers rollout, compatibility, backfill, rollback, and real database verification; it does not replace engine-specific design guidance.

capabilities.name: react-patterns
capabilities.trigger: React web component, hook, form, effect, state, or rendering-boundary work.
capabilities.guard: Do not use for React Native and do not assume a framework version before inspecting the repository.

capabilities.name: error-handling
capabilities.trigger: Typed errors, retry policy, failure contracts, circuit breakers, or safe user-facing failures.
capabilities.guard: Do not add retries or abstraction without evidence that the failure mode requires them.

capabilities.name: api-design
capabilities.trigger: REST resource naming, methods, status codes, pagination, filtering, errors, or versioning.
capabilities.guard: Governs HTTP semantics, not the backend's internal architecture.

capabilities.name: contract-first
capabilities.trigger: A boundary shared by independently evolving consumers and providers, or a breaking API/event change.
capabilities.guard: A private boundary changed atomically in one module usually needs only local types.

capabilities.name: backend-patterns
capabilities.trigger: Node.js, Express, or Next.js server routes and data-access structure.
capabilities.guard: Activate only after confirming one of its supported backend stacks.

capabilities.name: supabase-postgres-best-practices
capabilities.trigger: PostgreSQL schema, SQL, RLS, indexing, functions, triggers, connections, locks, or query performance.
capabilities.guard: Use for PostgreSQL anywhere; pair with database-migrations when persistent schema or data changes are involved.

capabilities.name: frontend-ui-engineering
capabilities.trigger: Production user-interface implementation with responsive states, interaction, forms, feedback, or integration.
capabilities.guard: Requires the actual frontend stack and existing design system; it does not define a new visual identity by itself.

capabilities.name: frontend-design
capabilities.trigger: A new interface or substantial redesign needs visual direction, hierarchy, typography, color, or interaction character.
capabilities.guard: Do not load for routine component edits or narrow polish.

capabilities.name: fixing-accessibility
capabilities.trigger: Explicit web accessibility work or a material web interaction involving focus, keyboard, forms, dialogs, semantics, or status feedback.
capabilities.guard: Web-only; use the optional native accessibility capability for React Native, iOS, or Android.

capabilities.name: react-testing
capabilities.trigger: Tests for React web components, hooks, pages, or user-visible component behavior.
capabilities.guard: Use the repository's configured runner and libraries; do not install a test stack just because this skill exists.

capabilities.name: security-best-practices
capabilities.trigger: An explicit security review, security report, or secure-by-default implementation in supported Python, JavaScript/TypeScript, or Go stacks.
capabilities.guard: Do not stack with redundant generic security reviews; HIGH or CRITICAL work still receives the main workflow's adversarial self-review.

capabilities.name: brand
capabilities.trigger: Brand voice, positioning, naming, identity consistency, or brand assets are explicit requirements.
capabilities.guard: Do not invent or replace brand policy without authoritative material or an explicit redesign request.

capabilities.name: ui-ux-pro-max
capabilities.trigger: A substantial experience needs journey design, information architecture, interaction strategy, or broad UX critique.
capabilities.guard: Do not load for a narrow styling fix; prefer one focused frontend skill when sufficient.

capabilities.name: react-native-patterns
capabilities.trigger: React Native or Expo screens, navigation, state, native APIs, lists, or platform behavior.
capabilities.guard: Do not apply React DOM assumptions or presume Expo Router and named libraries without repository evidence.

capabilities.name: shadcn
capabilities.trigger: The repository has shadcn evidence such as components.json or the user explicitly requests shadcn/ui.
capabilities.guard: Do not activate for generic React or Tailwind work and never run an @latest installer automatically.

capabilities.name: imagegen
capabilities.trigger: A raster image, illustration, texture, mockup, or image edit is explicitly requested or required by an accepted design.
capabilities.guard: Generate the asset only; Codex remains responsible for review, repository integration, and fresh verification.

capabilities.name: make-interfaces-feel-better
capabilities.trigger: An existing interface needs bounded polish to spacing, typography, borders, shadows, hit areas, or interaction states.
capabilities.guard: Use only if installed; do not turn a narrow polish task into a redesign.

capabilities.name: react-performance
capabilities.trigger: A measured React or Next.js performance problem involving waterfalls, bundles, rendering, or rerenders.
capabilities.guard: Use only with performance evidence or an explicit performance requirement; measure again after changes.

capabilities.name: vite-patterns
capabilities.trigger: Vite configuration, plugins, HMR, environment variables, SSR, library mode, or build behavior.
capabilities.guard: Use only if installed and after detecting the repository's actual Vite version.

capabilities.name: accessibility
capabilities.trigger: Native or cross-platform accessibility for React Native, iOS, or Android.
capabilities.guard: Use only if installed; do not substitute the web-focused accessibility workflow.

capabilities.name: motion-ui
capabilities.trigger: Motion is explicitly requested or the project already has a motion system that the change must follow.
capabilities.guard: Use only if installed; preserve reduced motion and avoid decorative animation without purpose.

capabilities.name: browser-qa
capabilities.trigger: A significant UI change has a runnable browser preview requiring bounded interaction, responsive, console, network, or visual checks.
capabilities.guard: Use only if installed and a runnable preview is available; report unavailable browser evidence honestly.

capabilities.name: e2e-testing
capabilities.trigger: A critical user journey needs an end-to-end regression and the repository already has an E2E framework.
capabilities.guard: Use only if installed; do not add an E2E framework for a change better covered at a lower level.

capabilities.name: click-path-audit
capabilities.trigger: A UI action races, reverts, duplicates, or disappears across handlers, stores, effects, persistence, or navigation.
capabilities.guard: Use only if installed and after systematic reproduction; this is a specialized trace, not a second general debugger.

capabilities.name: production-audit
capabilities.trigger: A real release or production-readiness decision requires operational, security, data, rollback, and journey evidence.
capabilities.guard: Use only if installed and for a real target; ordinary implementation does not need a production audit.

capabilities.name: architecture-decision-records
capabilities.trigger: A consequential architecture decision is difficult to reverse or affects several components.
capabilities.guard: Use only if installed; do not create ADRs for routine implementation choices.

capabilities.name: living-docs-governance
capabilities.trigger: A long-lived repository has demonstrated documentation drift or unclear canonical documents.
capabilities.guard: Use only if installed; do not introduce documentation governance for a one-off task.

capabilities.name: inherit-legacy-style
capabilities.trigger: An explicitly legacy, hand-written codebase has unclear conventions or observed style drift.
capabilities.guard: Use only if installed and from representative local evidence; never create global memory from it.

capabilities.name: codebase-onboarding
capabilities.trigger: The repository is unfamiliar and its entry points, boundaries, commands, or common change paths are unclear.
capabilities.guard: Use only if installed; ordinary targeted project discovery remains mandatory and usually sufficient.

overlap_rules.rule: Use systematic-debugging as the sole general debugging workflow. Add click-path-audit only for a reproduced UI state-flow problem.
Use repository checks during work and verification-before-completion as the final evidence gate. Production-audit is reserved for a real release decision.
database-migrations governs change lifecycle; supabase-postgres-best-practices governs PostgreSQL design and SQL. Use both for PostgreSQL migrations.
api-design governs HTTP semantics, contract-first governs independently evolving boundaries, and backend-patterns governs supported server implementation.
ui-ux-pro-max covers broad journeys, frontend-design covers visual direction, frontend-ui-engineering implements, framework skills refine stack behavior, and browser-qa verifies.
fixing-accessibility is for web; accessibility is optional and native. Select by platform rather than loading both.
Use security-best-practices as the specialist review when its trigger matches. Do not stack redundant generic security skills; HIGH and CRITICAL work gets one fresh adversarial self-review.
brand defines identity constraints, frontend-design applies visual direction, imagegen creates raster assets, and Codex integrates and verifies them.
